# 1 · Prerequisites & Access {.unnumbered}

This guide gets the control plane ready: the identities, permissions, network
paths, and software that every later step depends on. Nothing here writes
OrgPath — it makes the *later* writes possible and auditable.

## 1.1 Tenant & licensing

| Requirement | Why | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Microsoft Entra ID tenant (GCC-Moderate) | Holds device objects + extension attributes | Commercial infra, FedRAMP-Moderate authorized (ADR-033) |
| Entra ID P1 (P2 recommended) | Dynamic groups, Conditional Access targeting | P2 if you later adopt the reserved governance adapters |
| Microsoft Intune | MDM for Entra-joined clients (device-plane consumer) | Device writeback targets the device object, not Intune directly |
| Azure subscription with Azure Arc | Hosts `Microsoft.HybridCompute/machines` for servers | Required only for the Arc-server writeback (Guide 6) |

::: {.callout-note}
OrgPath writes facet values onto the **directory object** (Entra device) or the
**ARM resource** (Arc machine). Intune and Azure Policy then *target* those
values. You do not need the Intune-authoring or Policy-for-Arc adapters to run
the device-plane writeback — those are separate, reserved capabilities.
:::

## 1.2 Entra app registration (client credentials)

The CLI authenticates app-only (OAuth2 client-credentials) via MSAL. Create one
app registration; it serves both the Graph (Intune/Entra) and ARM (Arc) planes.

1. **Register an application** in Entra ID (single tenant).
2. **Add a credential** — a client secret *or* (preferred) a certificate.
3. **Record** the Tenant ID, Client ID, and the secret/cert.

### Graph application permissions (for the Entra device plane)

Grant **application** permissions (not delegated), then **grant admin consent**:

| Permission | Used for |
|---|---|
| `Device.ReadWrite.All` | Writing `onPremisesExtensionAttributes` on device objects |
| `Directory.Read.All` | Resolving devices / reading directory state |

> Verify the minimal permission set against current Microsoft Learn before
> production — Graph permission requirements evolve. The CLI requests the
> Graph `…/.default` scope for the selected cloud, so admin-consented
> application permissions are what actually gate the write.

### Azure RBAC (for the Arc server plane)

ARM authorization is **role-based**, not Graph-application-permission based. The
same app registration (service principal) must hold a role that can write tags
on the target Arc resources:

- **Tags Contributor** (writes tags only — least privilege), or
- **Contributor** (broader) on the resource group / subscription scope holding
  the `Microsoft.HybridCompute/machines` resources.

Assign the role to the **service principal** of your app registration at the
narrowest scope that covers your Arc fleet.

## 1.3 Network egress

| Plane | Outbound to (illustrative) | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Auth | `login.microsoftonline.com` (commercial) / `login.microsoftonline.us` (gov) | MSAL token acquisition |
| Graph | `graph.microsoft.com` (commercial) / `graph.microsoft.us` (gov) | Entra device writes |
| ARM | `management.azure.com` (commercial) / `management.usgovcloudapi.net` (gov) | Arc tag writes |

Arc *agent* enrollment has its own egress matrix (`*.his.arc.azure.com`,
`*.guestconfiguration.azure.com`, `*.servicebus.windows.net`, …). The
`assess_fleet_arc_readiness` helper flags servers whose egress is unvalidated;
see Guide 6 and the endpoint list in
`uiao.adapters.modernization.active_directory.arc_readiness.ARC_EGRESS_ENDPOINTS`.
Always confirm against the current Microsoft Learn Arc network-requirements page.

## 1.4 Install the CLI

The live write path (httpx + MSAL) ships in the `[api]` optional extra:

```bash
pip install "uiao[api]"
# dev/test tooling as well:
pip install -e ".[api,dev]"
```

Read-only assessment and dry-run governance work **without** the extra; only
the `--no-dry-run` dispatch needs httpx + msal.

## 1.5 Credentials in the environment

The token provider reads machine-level environment variables (never put these
in code or git):

```bash
export UIAO_ENTRA_TENANT_ID="<tenant-guid>"
export UIAO_ENTRA_CLIENT_ID="<app-client-id>"
# one of:
export UIAO_ENTRA_CLIENT_SECRET="<client-secret>"
#   or certificate auth:
export UIAO_ENTRA_CERT_PATH="/path/to/cert.pfx"
export UIAO_ENTRA_CERT_PASSWORD="<pfx-password>"   # omit for PEM
```

On the Windows/IIS deployment surface (`deploy/windows-server/`) set these as
**Machine-level** variables so the app pool inherits them.

## 1.6 Cloud selection

Every write command takes `--cloud`. The CLI derives the correct host **and**
token audience **and** login authority per cloud — a commercial-audience token
is rejected by sovereign endpoints (and a Graph-audience token is rejected by
ARM):

| `--cloud` | Graph host | ARM host | Login authority |
|---|---|---|---|
| `commercial` (also GCC-Moderate) | `graph.microsoft.com` | `management.azure.com` | `login.microsoftonline.com` |
| `gcc-high` | `graph.microsoft.us` | `management.usgovcloudapi.net` | `login.microsoftonline.us` |
| `dod` | `dod-graph.microsoft.us` | `management.usgovcloudapi.net` | `login.microsoftonline.us` |

## 1.7 Verify the install

```bash
uiao --version
uiao orgtree --help                 # validate codebook, assess, govern
uiao substrate walk                 # confirm the package tree is intact
```

If `uiao orgtree --help` lists `validate`, `assess`, and `govern`, the control
plane is ready. **Next:** [Author & validate the Codebook](02-codebook.qmd).
